description: Part XX (Article 368) of the Indian Constitution deals with the procedure for amending the Constitution. Over the past decade, several historic amendments have been enacted concerning taxation, social justice, and women's empowerment.

sections.title: 100th and 101st Constitutional Amendments
sections.description: These amendments deal with the territorial exchange with Bangladesh and the introduction of a nationwide indirect tax regime.

polity_articles.provision: Operationalized the Land Boundary Agreement (LBA) between India and Bangladesh.
polity_articles.details: India transferred 111 enclaves to Bangladesh and received 51 enclaves, requiring an amendment to the First Schedule of the Constitution.

polity_articles.provision: Introduction of the Goods and Services Tax (GST).
polity_articles.details: Inserted new Articles 246A (Special provision with respect to GST), 269A (Levy and collection of GST in the course of inter-state trade), and 279A (GST Council).

key_associations.extra_info: The GST Council is a joint forum of the Centre and States, chaired by the Union Finance Minister, which makes recommendations on GST rates and exemptions.

sections.title: 102nd and 103rd Constitutional Amendments
sections.description: These amendments focus on institutionalizing backward class rights and providing economic reservations in education and employment.

polity_articles.provision: Granted Constitutional Status to the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC).
polity_articles.details: Inserted Articles 338B (Structure, duties, and powers of NCBC) and 342A (Power of the President to notify socially and educationally backward classes).

polity_articles.provision: Provided 10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS).
polity_articles.details: Amended Articles 15 and 16 (added clause 6) to permit reservations for EWS among the unreserved categories in educational institutions and public employment.

important_facts.fact: The 103rd Amendment breached the historical 50% reservation ceiling, which was later upheld as constitutionally valid by the Supreme Court in the Janhit Abhiyan case (2022).

sections.title: 104th and 105th Constitutional Amendments
sections.description: Provisions related to political reservations in legislatures and restoring the power of states to identify backward classes.

polity_articles.provision: Extended the reservation of seats for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies by another 10 years (up to 2030).
polity_articles.details: Amended Article 334. Importantly, it did not extend the provision for the nomination of Anglo-Indian community members, effectively abolishing it.

polity_articles.provision: Restored the power of State Governments to identify and specify Socially and Educationally Backward Classes (SEBCs).
polity_articles.details: Brought in to override a Supreme Court ruling (Maratha reservation case) that had interpreted the 102nd Amendment as stripping states of this power.

key_concepts.explanation: Prior to the 104th Amendment, the President could nominate 2 Anglo-Indian members to the Lok Sabha under Article 331, and Governors could nominate 1 member to State Assemblies under Article 333. This system has now been discontinued.

sections.title: 106th Constitutional Amendment
sections.description: The most recent and historic amendment aimed at ensuring adequate representation of women in India's top legislative bodies.

historical_events.significance: Passed as the 106th Constitutional Amendment, it guarantees a historic 33% reservation for women in legislative bodies.

polity_articles.provision: Reserves one-third (33%) of all seats for women in the Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies, and the National Capital Territory of Delhi.
polity_articles.details: Inserted Articles 330A, 332A, and 334A. The reservation will come into effect after a delimitation exercise is undertaken based on the first census post-enactment.

important_facts.fact: The 106th Constitutional Amendment Bill was the first-ever legislation to be introduced and passed in the newly constructed Parliament building of India.

sections.title: Procedure and Types of Amendment
sections.description: Basic methods and parliamentary requirements to amend the Constitution of India under Article 368.

key_concepts.explanation: Most constitutional amendments require a majority of the total membership of the House AND a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting.

Amendments affecting the federal structure of the Constitution (like GST - 101st Amendment) require a Special Majority in Parliament plus ratification by the legislatures of at least half of the States by a simple majority.

important_facts.fact: A Constitutional Amendment Bill can be introduced in either House of Parliament (Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha), but there is absolutely no provision for a joint sitting of both Houses in case of a deadlock.
